# Singleton code wave: CR, in-place repair, SR→CR re-review, and fold

Constants:

- **Checkout:** `/workspace/project`. This is an integrated review, so `FD_ROOT` is the branch checkout.
- **Base:** `WAVE_BASE_SHA=1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. It stays fixed until the commit.
- **Scoped tests:** `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs`

## 1. Initial CR (one per code wave, over the integrated diff)

Stage all deliverables:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Record the CR tree for this wave. Call the printed SHA **T0**. On a nonzero exit, stop dispatch and report the error.

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Dispatch the initial CR:

```ts
subagent({ agent: "code-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project", task: `
<code-reviewer.md filled>
DESCRIPTION: Task 1 — <implementer summary>
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <full Task 1 text>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
+ per-file responsibility / plan structure / growth checks` })
```

This is a first review, so it has no re-review marker and no `TRAJECTORY:` line. It carries no `acceptance` field.

## 2. Supplied report → repair

The supplied report is `FIX_FIRST`, with one Moderate and `Behaviour-change: yes`. Routing:

- **Worker shape:** this is an integrated wave before its accepted-wave commit. It gets one plain in-place repair worker, with no fan-out and no nested wave.
- **Counting:** this is fix 1.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "implementer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project", task: `
<full Task 1 text + context>
## Previous review report (verbatim)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
TEST_CONTRACT: <Task 1 Tests: block + Files: paths verbatim>
Report Status: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT` })
```

The payload contains no commit or staging instruction.

**Observation:** the worker returned `DONE` and committed at `2222222…`, so HEAD has moved. That commit does not matter here:

- Worker commits do not affect the fix delta.
- `WAVE_BASE_SHA` stays `1111…`.
- I do not use a `1111..2222` SHA range or a working-tree diff in place of the tree delta.

Scoped gate (observed passing):

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs)
```

## 3. Repair-only delta

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# run the fix-delta-tree block again → T1
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T0> <T1>
```

The delta should contain only:

- the `src/parse.mjs` empty-string rejection, and
- the new `tests/error.test.mjs`.

## 4. SR first (behaviour-change reroute)

- The SR's ordinal continues the task's SR loop. The initial SR was review 1, so this is **SR review 2**.
- It is dispatched as a first review: no `## Previous review report` marker, so no `TRAJECTORY:` line.
- It does carry `## Fix delta`.
- This is a post-integration SR, so it reviews the implementation worktree directly. No snapshot is needed.
- It runs no tests.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "spec-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project", task: `
<full Task 1 text>
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10 (read the anchored range yourself)
Tests: <Task 1 Tests: block verbatim>   Test: tests/parse.test.mjs
Review the fix diff; read touched files in full; never run tests.
## Fix delta
<git diff --binary T0 T1 output>` })
```

**Observation:** the SR verdict is `COMPLIANT`.

## 5. CR re-review

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# run the fix-delta-tree block again → T2 (keyed to the wave)
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T0> <T2>
```

T0 is the prior CR's dispatch tree.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "code-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project", task: `
<code-reviewer.md filled, same as §1>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes
<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md, verbatim>
## Fix delta
<git diff --binary T0 T2 output>` })
```

- `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE` makes the reviewer diff the current checkout against `1111…`. That covers the worker's commit plus anything staged.
- CR round numbering is unchanged, so this is CR review 2.

**Observation:** the CR verdict is `SHIP`. A clean review ends the loop.

## 6. Fold commit, then tracker

Commit only after SR `COMPLIANT` and CR `SHIP`:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 \
  && git -C /workspace/project add -A \
  && git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Task 1: parse numbers; reject empty string"
```

- The soft reset folds the worker's `2222…` commit and the staged changes into one wave commit on `1111…`.
- If the commit comes out empty, stop and do not complete the task.
- On success, the tree is left clean for the next wave.

```ts
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: <Task 1 index>, status: "complete" })
```

## Empty repair delta

If `git diff --binary T0 T1` were empty, the fix changed no tracked file. That includes a repair that only touched ignored files, and it can happen even though the worker reported `DONE` and moved HEAD. In that case:

- Dispatch no SR or CR re-review.
- Count it as a failed attempt under "When a Subagent Fails".
- Re-send the prior report verbatim with "your fix changed no tracked file".
- Stop after the two-attempt limit. The task stays `in_progress` pending a human decision.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
The following are proposed commands and payloads, not execution results. Let `TASK_1` mean the available full Task 1 text, including its verbatim `**Tests:**` block, `- Test:` paths, and `Spec:` anchors. Expand it in dispatch payloads; do not substitute a summary.

### 1. Stage and capture the initial CR tree

Run in the branch checkout, preserving the fixed wave base even if a worker later commits:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A

FD_ROOT=/workspace/project
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Record the printed tree as `CR_TREE_1`. Stop dispatch on failure.

Initial review:

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Use the supplied requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md template.
DESCRIPTION: Integrated Task 1 implementation; initial SR accepted and scoped tests passed.
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
${TASK_1}
Authoritative spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
Review production readiness, including staged and unstaged changes against BASE_SHA.
`
})
```

The review source is the current checkout, **not** `BASE..HEAD`; initially HEAD alone contains none of the integrated patch.

### 2. Repair the supplied `FIX_FIRST`

Because this is an uncommitted integrated wave, use one in-place worker—not an isolated worktree or fan-out:

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Repair Task 1 in this checkout.
${TASK_1}
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10

Prior review report, verbatim:
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes

Verify the finding, reject empty-string input, and add the requested coverage.
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
Run only that scoped command for verification. Self-review.
Return explicitly DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT, or BLOCKED,
with changes, test-contract results, and concerns.
`
})
```

No commit or staging instruction belongs in this repair payload.

Consume the supplied observation: the worker returns `DONE` and has committed at `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`. Do **not** replace `WAVE_BASE_SHA` with that commit.

Run the scoped gate:

```bash
(cd /workspace/project && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs)
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

After its supplied passing result, run the **entire tree-capture block above again** and record its printed tree as `SR_TREE_2`. Produce the repair-only delta using the recorded tree SHAs:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <CR_TREE_1> <SR_TREE_2>
```

This captures the repair despite the worker’s commit. Do not use a commit range or working-tree-only diff.

### 3. Behavior-change SR first, then CR

Dispatch SR against the **integrated checkout**:

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "spec-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
${TASK_1}
Authoritative spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
Review the behavior-changing repair against those anchors.
## Fix delta
${REPAIR_ONLY_BINARY_DIFF}

Start from diff hunks carrying file:line; read every touched file in full.
Read deleted files from 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 if needed.
Never execute tests. The task's Tests block and Test paths above are contractual.
`
})
```

This is a first review of the behavior-changing repair: **no previous-report marker and no trajectory instruction**. Its SR ordinal continues Task 1’s existing SR count.

Only after the supplied `COMPLIANT` observation:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Run the entire capture block again, recording `CR_TREE_2`, then:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <CR_TREE_1> <CR_TREE_2>
```

Dispatch:

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Use the supplied code-reviewer template.
DESCRIPTION: Task 1 with empty-string rejection repair; repair SR is COMPLIANT.
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
${TASK_1}
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes

${VERBATIM_TRAJECTORY_BLOCK_FROM_SUPPLIED_CODE_QUALITY_REVIEWER_TEMPLATE}

## Fix delta
${BINARY_DIFF_CR_TREE_1_TO_CR_TREE_2}
`
})
```

Expand the trajectory placeholder with the supplied template’s complete re-review trajectory instructions, unchanged.

### 4. Commit only after the supplied `SHIP`

Fold the worker commit and all deliverables into one wave commit:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 &&
git -C /workspace/project add -A &&
git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Fix number parsing and cover empty input"
```

Only if that nonempty commit succeeds:

```ts
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: 1, status: "complete" })
```

Stop here.

An **empty repair tree delta** means no tracked deliverable changed. Dispatch no re-review; count a failed attempt and resend the prior report with “your fix changed no tracked file,” subject to the existing two-attempt limit.
